Balanced but cautious. The statement notes solid activity and still-strong, if moderating, job gains alongside low unemployment, while acknowledging inflation has eased but remains above target. Holding the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50% and maintaining quantitative tightening aligns with the forward‑looking policy prescriptions in Clarida–Galí–Gertler and Taylor‑rule frameworks, which call for staying restrictive until forecasts show inflation converging to 2%. The “greater confidence” language is consistent with Svensson and Woodford’s inflation‑forecast targeting emphasis and helps mitigate classic inflation‑bias/time‑inconsistency risks by reinforcing commitment to the 2% goal. With unemployment near its natural rate and a New Keynesian Phillips Curve backdrop, upside inflation risks persist, justifying a risk‑management stance reminiscent of “inflation‑at‑risk” thinking. Operationally, using interest on reserves and standing facilities reflects the post‑2008 floor‑system literature, while balance‑sheet runoff of Treasuries and agency MBS tightens financial conditions via term premia and housing channels noted in research linking yield‑curve factors (e.g., Cochrane–Piazzesi) and MBS to policy transmission. Net tone: moderately positive on real activity, cautious-to-hawkish on inflation.
